$description: The glass layer (decision 0004): very clear frosted glass on floating chrome and overlays only, with a guaranteed contrast floor. The tint (75%, decision 0021) is firm enough that on-surface text on the glass meets WCAG AA over any backdrop, for every seed (checked by scripts/check-glass.mjs). High contrast, reduced transparency and browsers without backdrop-filter make glass solid.

tint.$description: The surface role glass is tinted with.

float.$description: App bars over scrolled content, nav bar, nav rail, toolbars, menus, sheets, dialogs, rich tooltips.

fill.$description: Tonal fills inside a glass surface (no blur of their own).

tint-opacity.$description: How much of the tint role is painted over the blurred backdrop (0–1).

float.$description: Decision 0021: 75%, picked by the owner in the Glass Playground (was 0.6).

fab.$description: Decision 0028: the owner's pick, the same 75% as the other glass. A floating action button is glass tinted with its own color. The icon keeps 4.5:1 or better in monochrome; with a seed the opaque FAB color pair is only 4.5:1 in the worst schemes, so over pure black or white directly behind it a few seeds drop to about 2.3:1 (scripts/check-glass.mjs reports it).

medium-contrast.$description: Float tint when the app runs at medium contrast (contrast level 0.5).

fab-color.$description: Decision 0032: floating buttons in a color other than the default (secondary, tertiary, primary, or a container of those) are tinted 90%. Their own color pair is lower contrast than the default's, and at 75% the page checker found labels at 2.9:1 and 3.6:1 over a pure black or white backdrop. The default FAB keeps the owner's 75%.

float.$description: Backdrop blur radius. Decision 0021: 8px (owner's playground pick; was 16px).
saturate() on the backdrop. Decision 0021: 150% (owner's playground pick; was 120% in 0014).

contrast() on the backdrop. 1 (off) since decision 0021: the 75% tint alone keeps on-surface text at 4.5:1 or better over pure black or white (check-glass). Lower it below 1 only if the tint is lowered.
brightness() on the backdrop. 1 (off) since decision 0021, see backdrop-contrast.

max-stack.$description: At most two glass layers overlap at any point (e.g. a menu over an app bar). A third becomes solid.

item-fill.$description: How much of its own color an item (button, chip, text field) keeps on glass, 1 = fully (decision 0015: owner picked full fill; lower it to let the blurred backdrop tint items).

item-outline.$description: The outline of an outline-only item on glass (outlined button, unselected chip): the glass's milky frost line, a little stronger than the edge (decision 0015). Zero in high contrast, where glass is solid and the item keeps its own outline.

edge.$description: The glass edge (decisions 0021, 0027, 0031, 0033, 0034), calibrated against the iOS tab bar: a thin light rim along the top and the bottom that fades out around the curves and is absent on the sides, in the surface's own color lifted toward white (`lift`). The rim is a crescent drawn with an inset shadow that is offset up or down, so it follows the corner radius and is brightest on the flat part and the start of the curve. All zero where glass is solid.

line.$description: The single line full-width bars draw on their content-facing edge.

scale-standard.$description: Decision 0029: on a standard-density screen (under 1.5 device pixels per CSS pixel, e.g. a 1080p or 1440p monitor) the edge width is multiplied by this, so it stays visible. Retina and phone screens keep the width as it is.

scale-large.$description: Edge width multiplier on a large standard-density screen (a 2200px or wider display at under 1.5 device pixels per CSS pixel, e.g. 1440p and up).

top-alpha.$description: How strong the light line along the top edge is (0 to 1). Its color comes from the surface (see `lift`), never pure white.

side-alpha.$description: How strong the faint line all round is (0 to 1).

bottom-alpha.$description: How strong the light line along the bottom edge is (0 to 1). Lit like the top (decision 0033), in the same surface-based color, so a surface looks evenly lit and not raised.

lift.$description: Decision 0031: the edge light is the surface's own color moved this far toward white (0 = the surface color, 1 = pure white). A pale glass gets a near-white line; a dark glass or a dark floating button gets a softer, lighter version of itself instead of a hard white line.

glow.$description: The surface itself is a little lighter near the top and bottom edges and fades to its normal tone inside (decisions 0030, 0034; iOS: about +5% over 8 to 10px). Each side's glow is its edge color and alpha times `amount`, so it vanishes where the edge does. 0 is off.

amount.$description: How much of each edge's light is carried inward as glow: 0 is off, 1 repeats the edge's own strength, 2 doubles it (capped at fully opaque).

size.$description: How far the glow reaches inward from each edge.
